daily_brief: The Nepal-Tibet flood disaster dominates international headlines as the death toll surpasses 1,000 with over 4,400 people still missing, including hundreds of workers believed trapped in hydropower tunnels [BBC World, ABC Australia, Globe and Mail]. Rescue teams from Nepal, China, India, and other nations are racing against time to reach survivors, with one Australian found alive after six days [ABC Australia]. Meanwhile, Russia escalated its aerial bombardment of Ukraine overnight, killing at least 12 people in Kyiv and surrounding regions, including an Indian national, as EU defence ministers convene in Ireland to discuss bolstering Ukraine's air defences amid interceptor missile shortages [BBC Europe, Al Jazeera, RFI English, The Hindu]. In a landmark verdict, a Las Vegas jury found former gang leader Duane 'Keffe D' Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur, closing one of America's most infamous cold cases after nearly 30 years [BBC World, RNZ, Globe and Mail]. Iceland narrowly rejected resuming EU membership talks in a referendum, with 52.8% voting against despite security concerns raised by the government [BBC Europe]. In other developments, the Metropolitan Museum of Art cancelled its planned 2027 Met Gala honouring designer John Galliano following outcry over his 2011 antisemitic remarks [RNZ].

top_stories.headline: Nepal-Tibet Flood Death Toll Exceeds 1,000 as Rescuers Race to Reach Trapped Tunnel Workers
bullets: Death toll in Nepal alone reaches 987, with at least 16 confirmed deaths on the Chinese side; over 4,400 people remain missing across both countries
More than 600 workers are believed trapped in mud-filled tunnels at hydropower sites along Nepal's Trishuli River, with rescue teams pumping air into tunnels
International rescue teams from China, India, South Korea, and Australia are assisting Nepalese authorities despite challenging terrain and damaged infrastructure
One of 43 missing Australians was found alive in Tibet after six days; 42 Australians and 583 total foreign nationals remain unaccounted for

top_stories.headline: Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Kills 12 in Kyiv Region as EU Ministers Meet on Air Defence
bullets: At least 12 people killed and over 20 injured in overnight attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas, including six railway workers at a depot
An Indian citizen was among those killed; residential buildings in Boryspil suburb damaged with 50 people evacuated
Russia described the strikes as targeting military and energy facilities; Ukraine's Zelenskyy condemned 'Russian terror' and called for stronger air defences
EU defence ministers convening in Ireland to discuss Ukraine's air defence shortages amid concerns over depleted interceptor missile stockpiles

top_stories.headline: Former Gang Leader Found Guilty of Orchestrating Tupac Shakur's 1996 Murder
bullets: Las Vegas jury convicted Duane 'Keffe D' Davis, 63, of first-degree murder with a deadly weapon after nearly three hours of deliberation
Davis was accused of ordering the drive-by shooting and supplying the gun used by his nephew Orlando Anderson, who died in 1998
Prosecution relied heavily on Davis's own media appearances and memoir, plus recorded police interviews where he admitted being in the car
Davis faces potential life imprisonment without parole; he announced plans to appeal the verdict

top_stories.headline: Iceland Rejects Resuming EU Membership Talks in Close Referendum
bullets: 52.8% of voters rejected the government's proposal to restart EU accession talks, with approximately 12,600 votes separating the two sides
Turnout was 82.5%, the highest in any Icelandic election since 2009, with over 225,000 people casting ballots
Prime Minister Kristrún Frostadóttir's government had advanced the referendum citing international tensions, including Trump's threats against Greenland
Debate centred primarily on fishing rights rather than security concerns; Iceland froze its EU application in 2013 over fisheries disputes

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Provided historical context on Iceland's 2009 application and Cod Wars history; neutral presentation of both sides

top_stories.headline: Metropolitan Museum Cancels 2027 Met Gala Honouring Designer John Galliano After Antisemitism Outcry
bullets: The museum reversed its decision to make controversial designer John Galliano the subject of an exhibit linked to the 2027 Met Gala
Galliano was fired from Dior in 2011 and convicted of 'public insults' after videos emerged of him making antisemitic remarks including 'I love Hitler'
The 2027 Met Gala would have fallen on Yom HaShoah, a day of Holocaust remembrance, intensifying criticism
Galliano released a statement saying he did not want debate surrounding him to place the Met in a difficult position

sources.name: RNZ
sources.framing_note: Detailed reporting on the controversy and Galliano's history; included his apology statement
